# Capabilities

Everything Workbench can run, as registered. The Agent reaches the same list: an id shown here is a name it can use in a proposal or a workflow step.

## Model families (22)

| Id | What it does |
|---|---|
| `model.anova` | Factorial analysis of variance with optional covariates. Declares its sums-of-squares type explicitly: SPSS reports Type III and R's aov reports Type I, and on an unbalanced design they disagree. |
| `model.cs_did` | Heterogeneity-robust group-time ATT(g,t) with event-study, group, and calendar aggregations and simultaneous confidence bands. Eliminates the staggered-adoption bias of TWFE DID. |
| `model.dcdh` | Dynamic DID for binary NON-ABSORBING (switching) treatment using not-yet-switched controls (de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille). Handles treatments that turn on and off, which Callaway-Sant'Anna and Sun-Abraham cannot. Event study with native placebo pre-trend tests. |
| `model.did` | Two-way fixed-effects DID with event study, parallel-trends test, and Goodman-Bacon decomposition. |
| `model.glm:binomial` | Generalized linear model with binomial family. |
| `model.glm:negative_binomial` | Generalized linear model with negative binomial family. |
| `model.glm:poisson` | Generalized linear model with Poisson family. |
| `model.iv_2sls` | Two-stage least squares with instrumental variables for endogenous regressors. |
| `model.linear_mixed_effects` | Repeated-measures linear mixed model with explicit subject, time, and group roles. |
| `model.logit` | Logistic regression for binary outcomes. |
| `model.multinomial_logit` | Nominal categorical outcome with probabilities, relative-risk ratios, and marginal effects. |
| `model.negative_binomial` | For overdispersed count outcomes. |
| `model.ols` | Ordinary Least Squares with HC1 robust SE. |
| `model.ordinal_logit` | Ordered categorical outcome with logit or probit link, probabilities, odds ratios where applicable, marginal effects, and a parallel-lines diagnostic. |
| `model.panel_ols` | Fixed/random effects panel OLS. |
| `model.poisson` | Poisson regression for count outcomes. |
| `model.probit` | Probit regression for binary outcomes. |
| `model.quantile_regression` | Multiple conditional quantiles with confidence intervals, optional bootstrap intervals, and cross-quantile comparisons. |
| `model.sa_did` | Interaction-weighted event-study estimator (Sun & Abraham 2021). Heterogeneity-robust dynamic ATT using clean-control cohorts, immune to the contamination of TWFE event-study leads/lags under staggered adoption. |
| `model.survival_cox` | Cox proportional-hazards model with Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, risk-set, censoring, and Schoenfeld evidence. |
| `model.time_series.arma_garch` | Execute time_series.arma_garch through its registered model pack. |
| `model.time_series.ets` | Execute time_series.ets through its registered model pack. |

## Statistical tests (8)

| Id | What it does |
|---|---|
| `test.anova` | One-way ANOVA of a numeric outcome across a categorical group with three or more levels. |
| `test.chi_square` | Chi-square test of independence between two categorical columns. |
| `test.correlations` | Pearson correlation for every pair of numeric analysis columns. |
| `test.evidence` | Advanced evidence packet: effect sizes, ANOVA post-hoc comparisons, variance tests, and paired or one-sample tests for declared targets. |
| `test.fisher_exact` | Fisher exact test of independence, for tables too sparse for the chi-square approximation. |
| `test.nonparametric` | Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis rank tests, for group differences without a normality assumption. |
| `test.rank_correlations` | Spearman and Kendall rank correlation, for monotonic association that is not linear. |
| `test.t_tests` | Welch two-sample t-test of a numeric outcome across a binary group. |

## Prediction models (3)

| Id | What it does |
|---|---|
| `prediction.prediction_lasso` | L1-regularized linear prediction. Execute the bounded out-of-sample prediction protocol. |
| `prediction.prediction_random_forest` | Tree-ensemble prediction. Execute the bounded out-of-sample prediction protocol. |
| `prediction.prediction_ridge` | L2-regularized linear prediction. Execute the bounded out-of-sample prediction protocol. |

## Data preparation (4)

| Id | What it does |
|---|---|
| `imputation.mice` | Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations. Recommended when more than 5-10% of rows would otherwise be dropped due to missing values. |
| `resample.oversample` | Resample prediction-training data with Oversample. |
| `resample.smote` | Resample prediction-training data with SMOTE. |
| `resample.undersample` | Resample prediction-training data with Undersample. |

## Operations (34)

| Id | What it does |
|---|---|
| `code.execute` | Run a Python transformation in the sandbox against the current dataset node (read df and produce result), creating a child dataset node; the source is read-only, network access is disabled, and resources are limited. |
| `data.aggregate` | Aggregate rows by declared groups and named functions. Example spec: {"aggregations": [{"column": "wage", "func": "mean", "output": "mean_wage"}], "group_by": ["region"]} |
| `data.append` | Append a declared secondary dataset with an explicit schema policy. Example spec: {"schema_policy": "exact", "secondary_artifact_id": "raw_b.csv", "secondary_node_id": "stage:raw", "secondary_run_id": "run_b"} |
| `data.column.cast` | Cast one existing column in the current dataset node to a supported target type. |
| `data.columns.cast` | Cast multiple existing columns in the current dataset node in one operation, producing one child dataset node. |
| `data.dedupe` | Remove duplicate rows using an explicit key and keep policy. Example spec: {"columns": ["id"], "keep": "first"} |
| `data.feature_recipe` | Create one typed feature recipe child from the registered recipe vocabulary. |
| `data.fill_missing` | Resolve missing values with an explicit per-column strategy. Example spec: {"strategies": [{"column": "hours", "strategy": "median"}]} |
| `data.lag` | Create deterministic lag columns from an ordered dataset. Example spec: {"columns": ["gdp"], "lags": [1]} |
| `data.merge` | Merge the current dataset with a declared secondary dataset. Example spec: {"how": "left", "keys": ["id"], "secondary_artifact_id": "raw_b.csv", "secondary_node_id": "stage:raw", "secondary_run_id": "run_b"} |
| `data.recode` | Recode one variable into a NEW variable by ordered rules (SPSS RECODE INTO): single values, closed numeric ranges {low, high}, "missing", and a final "else". First matching rule wins; to: a code, null (missing) or "copy". Values no rule covers are refused unless an else rule exists. Example spec: {"column": "age", "output": "age_group", "rules": [{"from": {"high": 39, "low": 18}, "to": 1}, {"from": {"high": 120, "low": 40}, "to": 2}, {"from": "missing", "to": 9}]} |
| `data.rename` | Rename existing columns with collision-checked mapping. Example spec: {"mapping": {"inc": "income"}} |
| `data.reshape` | Reshape the current dataset with an explicitly declared direction. Example spec: {"direction": "wide_to_long", "id_columns": ["id"], "value_columns": ["y2020", "y2021"], "value_name": "income", "var_name": "year"} |
| `data.subset` | Subset rows and columns with closed comparison operators. Example spec: {"columns": ["id", "age"], "filters": [{"column": "age", "op": "between", "value": [25, 55]}]} |
| `data.tsset` | Declare and stably order a time or panel-time index. Example spec: {"frequency": "Y", "time_column": "year"} |
| `graph.fork` | Create a new Chain branch from the current verified node. |
| `metadata.edit` | Declare or change variable labels, value labels, measurement levels or missing-value codes for any column. Never changes which variables are in the model; the run is re-estimated with the new metadata (missing codes change the sample). |
| `model.custom` | Run one explicitly admitted custom capability through the Proposal/Risk and containment gates. |
| `model.genesis` | Create a first-run model Draft from a verified dataset source. |
| `model.joint_f_test` | Run a joint F test over terms already present in a completed, unadjusted OLS branch. |
| `model.quadratic_stationary_point` | Compute -beta_linear / (2 * beta_square) only when both declared terms are present in a completed quadratic OLS branch. |
| `model.rerun` | Change the current model parameters and rerun. |
| `model.white_test` | Run White's test for heteroskedasticity on a completed OLS branch. |
| `operation.multi_step` | Compile and execute a multi-step statistical workflow with one confirmation and auditable per-step artifacts. |
| `postestimation.lincom` | Estimate a linear combination of a completed model's coefficients, with its standard error, test and confidence interval. |
| `postestimation.lr` | Likelihood-ratio test of a restricted model nested in a fuller one. Both must be estimated on the same rows with model-based (not robust or clustered) variance. If the user's original model has robust, clustered or design-based variance, explain that LR uses the model likelihood and requires two new fits with model-based variance; keep the original model and actively offer a Wald test using its original covariance as an alternative. Do not automatically add a Wald step merely because the user asks you to offer that option; include it only when execution of Wald is requested. Fit both branches and then reference them in one plan with one confirmation. |
| `postestimation.margins` | Marginal effects of regressors on the predicted outcome: averaged over the estimation sample (`at: average`) or at the regressors' means (`at: means`). |
| `postestimation.nlcom` | Estimate a smooth function of a completed model's coefficients by the delta method. |
| `postestimation.wald` | Jointly test linear restrictions on a completed model's coefficients (Wald). Reads the model's stored covariance; F or chi-square follows the model's own inference. |
| `report.compose` | Assemble the completed steps into a report. |
| `statistical.derive_boolean` | Create one server-defined boolean grouping node. |
| `statistical.derive_numeric` | Create declared numeric columns without arbitrary code. |
| `statistical.derived_group_summarize` | Summarize columns within each derived group. |
| `statistical.explore` | Run one server-defined statistical exploration step. |
